title: Humayun The Bengal Campaign And Struggle With Sher Khan
definition: A critical phase in the early Mughal period (1537-1540) characterized by Humayun's strategic miscalculation in Bengal and the rise of Sher Khan Suri, leading to the temporary collapse of Mughal authority in India.
importanceInUpsc: This topic is essential for understanding the transition from the Mughal to the Sur Empire, the strategic importance of the Chunar and Gaur forts, and the military tactical superiority of Sher Khan over Humayun.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Humayun The Bengal Campaign And Struggle With Sher Khan.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Establishment of Mughal Empire by Babur
